V. ANY PROBABLE ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS WHICH CANNOT BE AVOIDED SHOULD THE PROPOSAL BE IMPLEMENTED
As required in Section 107.01 of the State of Illinois Department of Transportation Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, contractors for construction of the project shall at all times observe and comply with all Federal and State Laws, local laws, ordinances, and regulations which in any manner affect the conduct of the work.
A. Noise Pollution
There are no feasible, economic, nor prudent structural or vegetative land form noise abatement measures which could be incorporated into this proposed highway improvement project to meet the exterior design year noise standards for the developed lands along Lincoln Highway.
To use any structural noise abatement measures other than the proposed alignment and profile would not be in the interest of serving both State and local community goals. As a principal arterial, Lincoln Highway is a non-access controlled facility that not only serves as land access to the abutting property owners, but also serves to distribute traffic to the minor arterial system.
The minor arterial system interconnects with and augments the principal arterial system and provides service to trips of moderate length at a lower level of travel mobility. This system places more emphasis on land access and provides intra-community continuity.
Because both the principal and minor arterial systems serve as land access, to provide a noise barrier would have the following effects:
....Obstruct both pedestrian and driver vision resulting in a roadway that would have a greater potential accident rate.
.... Noise barriers within urban boundaries would be discontinuous in order to provide access to abutting properties. The line of sight is diminished resulting in a hazardous roadway condition and reduction in visual access to commercial and business facilities.
